reason: H0 can set SPNG_DECODE_PROGRESSIVE through its fuzzed flags, but after spng_decode_image returns from progressive initialization it immediately frees ctx and never drives the progressive row/scanline protocol. Therefore it misses the SPNG_STATE_DECODE_INIT-to-SPNG_STATE_EOI transition and the newly changed end-of-image handling in spng_decode_scanline, including discarding ctx->cur_chunk_bytes_left and updating ctx->last_idat.
evidence: H0 calls spng_decode_image(ctx, out, out_size, fmt, flags) exactly once and then reaches err, where it calls spng_ctx_free(ctx).
In spng_decode_image, flags & SPNG_DECODE_PROGRESSIVE causes an early return of 0 before the internal do/while loop that calls spng_decode_row.

The changed spng_decode_scanline branch executes only on the last scanline of ctx->last_pass, sets ctx->state = SPNG_STATE_EOI, calls discard_chunk_bytes(ctx, ctx->cur_chunk_bytes_left), and copies ctx->current_chunk to ctx->last_idat.
Non-progressive inputs reach spng_decode_scanline through spng_decode_image's spng_decode_row loop, but progressive inputs require additional public decode calls that H0 does not make.
recommended_action: Add a progressive-decode harness path that, after spng_decode_image(..., SPNG_DECODE_PROGRESSIVE) succeeds, repeatedly calls spng_decode_row or spng_decode_scanline with appropriately sized buffers until SPNG_EOI or another error, including both buffer-backed and stream-backed inputs.
